claims.text: Spin-polarized density functional theory can be used to predict and identify ferromagnetic ground states in multicomponent alloys, including high-entropy alloys.
Spin-polarized DFT explicitly accounts for electron spin and exchange interactions.
High-entropy alloys can occur as multicomponent solid solutions.
The proposed initial material is a disordered solid solution containing magnetic elements.
Total energies of multiple spin configurations can be determined using spin-polarized DFT.
Ground-state calculations should be performed at approximately 0 K.
The calculations use periodic boundary conditions.
The reliability of the magnetic prediction depends on using an exchange-correlation functional that adequately captures electron-correlation effects.
Spin-polarized DFT resolves spin-dependent electron densities and exchange splitting between spin-up and spin-down states.
Exchange interactions can lower the total energy when magnetic moments align.
An aligned-spin configuration is a ferromagnetic ground state when it has the lowest total energy among the tested configurations.
The predicted lowest-energy state will have finite magnetic moments aligned in the same direction.
The ferromagnetic state will be lower in energy than non-spin-polarized or antiferromagnetic configurations.
Non-spin-polarized DFT neglects explicit treatment of the spin degree of freedom.
Magnetic predictions can be sensitive to the choice of exchange-correlation functional.
Ground-state DFT calculations may not capture finite-temperature magnetic effects.
The proposed method is most reliable for predictions at 0 K.
Predicted magnetic moments and spin-configuration energy differences can vary with computational parameters and approximations.
Low-temperature SQUID magnetometry can provide experimental magnetization and hysteresis data for comparison with DFT predictions.
Failure to predict a lower-energy ferromagnetic state, or substantial disagreement with measured magnetic moments, would falsify the claimed reliability for the selected material.
